facts.fact: The article says Project BRIDGE, a 90,000 km national fibre build, is to reach all 774 local government areas and connect 3,400 local government offices, alongside 38,800 public schools and 16,900 health facilities, with completion targeted for 2028 or early 2029 as the communications minister announced on 22 September 2026.

The article puts development-finance commitments to Project BRIDGE at US$845 million (World Bank US$500m, African Development Bank US$200m approved April 2026, EBRD US$100m, a European Union grant of EUR 22m), with private capital sought through a special purpose vehicle; the minister said implementation funding is secured.

The article says Project BRIDGE is structured as a majority privately owned and managed project company providing wholesale open-access fibre, in which the Federal Government holds a minority stake capped at 49 per cent.

On 22 September 2026 the communications minister cut Project BRIDGE's delivery timeline from five years to three, with physical cable laying slated to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026; no local government office is yet stated to be connected by it.

systems.owner: special purpose vehicle, majority private, Federal Government stake capped at 49%
systems.tiers: planned: all 774 local government areas, 3,400 local government offices, 38,800 public schools, 16,900 health facilities; construction not begun
at least 200 towers due active before December 2026, each serving communities of 5,000 to 10,000 people

note: Capture ends mid-sentence. BRIDGE is classed connection here because the article says it will connect local government offices; that is a plan, not a live connection, and construction had not begun.
